**File: src/polyglot/main/Options.java**

Modification: In the `addBootCP` method, the way new boot classpath directories are added to the existing `bootclasspathDirectories()` list is changed. Previously, `value` elements were appended to the end of the list using `addAll(value)`. The patch changes this to `addAll(0, value)`, which inserts the new elements at the beginning of the list instead.

**Relationship:**
This is a single-file, single-method fix. The change affects the ordering semantics of boot classpath directories when they are added via `addBootCP`. By inserting new entries at the front rather than appending them at the end, entries added later (e.g., via command-line options processed in sequence) will take precedence (or be searched first) over previously added boot classpath directories. This ensures that the order in which boot classpath directories are specified is respected correctly, fixing a bug where newly specified boot classpath entries were incorrectly placed after existing ones, potentially causing incorrect class resolution order.

`bootclasspathDirectories().addAll(value);`
Reason: This appends each new batch of boot classpath directories to the end of the existing list. Since directories specified later are supposed to take precedence (i.e., be searched first), appending them instead of inserting them at the front causes the classpath order to become reversed. As a result, when multiple boot classpath additions are processed sequentially, the earlier-added directories remain at the front and get searched first, even though the later-added ones should have priority.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`bootclasspathDirectories().addAll(0, value);`
Reason: By inserting the new directories at index 0 instead of appending them at the end, each new call to `addBootCP` places its directories at the front of the list. This ensures that directories added later end up earlier in the classpath, correctly giving them precedence over previously added directories, matching the intended "last specified, first searched" semantics.
